propositions: The primary comment-dedup guard (is_comment_mapped keyed on comment_id) was silently inert in production because the comment_ids map in bindings.json remained empty from feature launch (2026-08-13) until the fix landed (2026-08-20), a 6-day window classified as never-worked rather than regression.

The fallback body-equality dedup skip absorbed enough successful deduplication (22/25 short comments) that the primary guard's failure appeared as partial success and flakiness rather than total failure, masking the defect.

Existing unit tests seed invariants at layer boundaries and never cross the seam between apply-phase recording and differ-phase skip logic, so they would still pass with is_comment_mapped hard-wired to False and could not detect the inert guard end-to-end.

Plan-review criteria E4, T3, T5b all abstain or stop short of blocking on the specific class of failure (external API response schema dependency, fail-open guard silently returning), and code-review fail-open detection was added post-escape only after multiple instances were observed in production.

No production observability existed to flag the invariant violation (comment_ids=0 while bindings>2475 and outbound posts succeeded), leaving the defect undetected despite committed evidence in production state throughout the escape window.

The silently-inert guard pattern—a secondary guard carrying traffic after a silent failure of a primary correctness-critical guard—survives review and test because each layer's tests seed the other's preconditions without crossing their boundary.
